agent.name: Flag
agent.strategy: Bull flag: pole, quiet drift, breakout
agent.description: Well-formed bull flags across the universe: forming flags with their trigger and stop, and breakouts on volume with the trade attached.

context.label: Well-formed
context.value: flag vol <= 70% of pole, pullback <= 40%, 5-8 sessions

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 20% pole · 6-session flag · 31% pullback on 43% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag's consolidation at only 31% of the pole's range is shallow—healthy flags typically retrace 38-50%—suggesting weak selling pressure and potentially incomplete pullback energy. The trigger ($83.22) is barely 0.2% above today's close, leaving almost no margin for the pattern to "set" before entry, which increases whipsaw risk; a break above $84.56 (the pole high) would confirm conviction, while closing below $80.22 on volume would decisively kill it. Given that forming flags historically underperform, this needs a clean daily close above the flag's upper boundary *and* a convincing break of $84.56 on volume to separate signal from noise.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 24% pole · 5-session flag · 32% pullback on 56% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag is structurally messy: the pole gained 4.3% but the retracement only fell 6.1%, leaving minimal space between the trigger ($155.03) and the flag floor ($148.50)—just 4.5%—which is tight risk/reward and suggests weak conviction in the prior move. setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 18% pole · 5-session flag · 33% pullback on 64% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This is a textbook flag structure on paper, but the volume compression (64% of pole volume) during the flag is concerning—it suggests weak conviction rather than orderly consolidation, and flags with slack volume tend to fail more than succeed. Confirmation would require a decisive break above $37.70 on volume matching or exceeding the pole; anything less is suspect. A close below $36.70 kills it outright, but even a weak push through the trigger without volume should be treated as a failed setup, not a trade.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 27% pole · 5-session flag · 31% pullback on 66% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning:
# ITRI Bull Flag Analysis

This flag is **structurally clean but momentum-poor**: the pullback is textbook (tight, orderly, reduced volume), but a 27% run followed by only a 5-session consolidation is thin air—most flags need 8–15 sessions to establish conviction. A break above $100.76 on volume >66% of the pole's average would confirm follow-through; any close back below $96.50 or a sixth+ session of listless ranging kills it, especially if the breakout attempt fizzles on lower volume than the pole itself.
